title: Kellen Moore reportedly expected to be hired as Saints' next head coach
text:
The offensive coordinator of the Philadelphia Eagles, Kellen Moore is expected ADAM SCHEFTER DE ESPN .
Moore, 36, would take care of a team from the Saints that ended 5-12 last season and ended in the last place in the south of the NFC. Chief coach Dennis Allen was fired after nine games and his replacement, Darren Rizzi, had 3-5 interim.
Before it is officially announced, Moore will help lead the Eagles against Kansas City chiefs at the Super Bowl Lix on Sunday.
Kellen Moore was able to enjoy the attention of the Super Bowl on Monday during the opening night with the media. (Photo by Jonathan Bachman/Getty Images)
After a NFL player of six stations with the Detroit Lions and the Dallas Cowboys, Moore entered the training ranges starting as a field marshal coach and then assumed the position of offensive coordinator with the 2019-2022 cowboys. After separating from Dallas, he took over the offensive of the Los Angeles Chargers as part of Brandon Staley’s staff, but it was just a season before being hired by the Philadelphia Eagles in the same position.
The Saints were the last NFL team that was left with a vacancy in the chief coach. General Manager Mickey Loomis launched a wide network in the search for a new chief coach. He spoke with Rizzi, Moore, Aaron Glenn, Joe Brady and Anthony Weaver, among others. Mike McCarthy was also a candidate, but according to the reports he retired from the race and will return to the training market by 2026.
The Saints have not reached the playoffs since 2020, the end of their four -year career as NFC South champions.
